title: 1983 AHSME Problem 4
statement: In the adjoining plane figure, sides \(AF\) and \(CD\) are parallel, as are sides \(AB\) and \(FE,\) and sides \(BC\) and \(ED.\) Each side has length \(1.\) Also, \(\angle FAB=\angle BCD=60^\circ.\) The area of the figure is

solutions.text:
The parallel directions and \(60^\circ\) angles place the vertices, up to rigid motion, at \[ \begin{aligned} A&=(0,0),\\ B&=(\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2},-\tfrac12),\\ C&=(\sqrt3,0),\\ D&=(\sqrt3,-1),\\ E&=(\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2},-\tfrac32),\\ F&=(0,-1). \end{aligned} \] Applying the shoelace formula to these six vertices gives area \(\sqrt3.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is D.
hints: Place \(AF\) and \(CD\) vertically and use the \(60^\circ\) angles to assign coordinates
The six vertices can be written using horizontal changes of \(\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\)
